newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts close higher, tracking Bunds.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts close higher, tracking Bunds.

text.p: UK gilt futures closed higher, taking their cue from Bunds in the absence of fresh domestic developments and with a market holiday in the U.S. Gilts could face a setback from strong UK October consumer credit data on Friday.
* Dec long gilt future closed 12/32 higher at 110-31/32
"Credit card borrowing is up strongly and stores have been opening record numbers of new accounts, so it looks like the personal sector is still borrowing quite strongly," Rayner said.
"This would be consistent with the view that demand is strong. If we do have a strong number tomorrow, it might hurt the short end of the market a little."

Several members of the Treasury's panel of independent economic advisers said demand was growing alarmingly strongly and called for higher interest rates. "Demand is now growing too rapidly," said panel member Gavyn Davies, also Goldman Sachs chief economist.
"The implication....is that interest rates have to go up further," he told the House of Commons Treasury Select Committee.

Tim Congdon, director of Lombard Street Research, told the committee: "The implied growth rates of domestic demand are for five percent a year, unless something else happens, which does amount effectively to boom rates of growth."
March short sterling was one basis point higher at 93.29, implying official rates of around 6.70 percent by the end of the first quarter compared with 6.0 percent now.
The gilt-Bund spread at 10 years was 183 basis points compared with 185 on Wednesday.
